about: Exceptions for scripts/security/secret-scan.mjs. A secret-rule entry only lets through values that look fake (fixture markers, a few distinct characters, a PEM body of a few bytes); a real key in the same file is still reported. Each entry needs a reason.

entries.reason: Service-account fixture whose PEM body is 4 characters, so it cannot be a key.

Scanner tests feed fake secrets to the scanner; secret rules still require the value to look fake. A '*' entry never covers client data or planning words: the entries below name those rules for each scanner test.
Made-up client addresses the scanner tests feed to the client-data rule.
Made-up client addresses the scan and client-data cleanup tests feed to the scanner and the cleanup.
Made-up client phone numbers the scan and client-data cleanup tests feed to the scanner and the cleanup.
Service-account-shaped fixture for the env quoting round trip; the PEM body is a few fake bytes.
Fake prod env values for the env-sync override tests; secret rules still require the value to look fake.
npm registry metadata that npm writes into the lockfile (a package maintainer contact inside a deprecation notice).

fixtureValuesAbout: Each entry lets one exact value through, by its sha256, in the matching paths only.

fixtureValues.reason: The sales booker's sign-in address that the booker assignment code matches. Allowed in this one runtime file only; tests import the constant.

commitEntriesAbout: Each entry lets one finding through in one past commit only (exact sha, path, line and rule). It never covers a value from a local .env file or a retired secret, and the scan lists every finding it lets through.

commitEntries.reason: Made-up ADMIN_SECRET fixture for the env-sync tests in an intermediate commit. It matches no local .env value and no retired secret, and the next change to that file (3d8f1b6) replaced it with a fake- value.
One-letter sample reply-to address in the cms-spec section merge test; the integration branch changed it to an example.no address.

An earlier version of this list allowed the sales booker's sign-in address in every file. The address was already public in the booker assignment code and its tests; it is now allowed in that code file only (fixtureValues).

emailsReason: Placeholder addresses only: Norwegian sample names on firma.no and an IDN sample in the LLM person-field detector tests and contract checks, a generic mailbox in the automation-settings validation test, the owner-routing input placeholder, the input placeholders of the sign-in, settings, staff, booking and checkout forms, the usage line of the inbox emulator and a comment about contact e-mails turned into links. Asoldi's own contact: the owner's address (the co-author identity in every commit and the default test-mail recipient).
phonesReason: Asoldi's own numbers: the company number and the sales rep number that is printed in every e-mail the rep sends (seeded for that rep in data/store.js).
